findings.title: Async legacy writes use the request context and will be cancelled when the request completes
findings.body: In Create (and identically in Delete line 110, Update line 135, and DeleteCollection line 163), the fire-and-forget goroutine derives its timeout context from the incoming request context (`ctx`). The Kubernetes apiserver cancels the request context as soon as the handler returns, and this function returns immediately after the storage write without waiting for the goroutine. As a result the legacy write will almost always run with an already-cancelled context and fail with context.Canceled, silently dropping the legacy copy that mode 3 is supposed to maintain 'as a safe measure'. The goroutine should derive from `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` (or a background context carrying the logger/values) before applying the 10s timeout.

findings.title: Storage create error is recorded as a legacy duration metric
findings.body: When `d.Storage.Create` fails, the code calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)` even though no legacy call was made; the failure occurred in unified storage. The same mistake exists in Update at line 129 (`recordLegacyDuration` on a `d.Storage.Update` error). This mislabels storage errors as legacy errors and records them against the storage start time, corrupting the dual-writer duration/error metrics that are presumably used to monitor the migration.

findings.title: Delete records storage duration metric with object name instead of kind label
findings.body: After a successful `d.Storage.Delete`, the code calls `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)` passing the object `name` where every other call site passes `options.Kind`. This creates a high-cardinality, inconsistent label value (per-object names) in the storage duration metric, both breaking aggregation by kind and potentially exploding the Prometheus series cardinality.

findings.title: DeleteCollection records legacy write duration under the storage metric
findings.body: Inside the async goroutine in DeleteCollection, the legacy call's outcome is recorded with `d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, ...)` instead of `recordLegacyDuration`. Legacy delete-collection latency and errors will be attributed to the unified storage metric, making the legacy metric silently empty and the storage metric wrong.

findings.title: Legacy update no longer stores the object produced by the storage update
findings.body: The previous implementation fetched the old object once, computed the updated object, ran the storage update, and then wrote the storage-produced object (`obj`) to legacy via an `updateWrapper`, guaranteeing both stores converge to the same content. The new code passes the original `objInfo` independently to both `Storage.Update` and (asynchronously) `Legacy.Update`, so `UpdatedObject` is evaluated twice against potentially different old objects, and any fields set by the storage layer during update (e.g. generated values, normalized fields) are never propagated to legacy. Legacy can silently diverge from unified storage, which defeats mode 3's purpose of keeping legacy as a consistent safety copy. Additionally the two updates race with any concurrent writer since legacy is now applied later, unordered, with no error logging.

findings.title: Legacy write failures are no longer logged
findings.body: The previous mode 3 implementation logged an error when a legacy Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection failed. The new async goroutines only record the failure in a metric (`recordLegacyDuration(errObjectSt != nil, ...)`) and never log it. During a migration where legacy is the fallback store, operators will have no log trail explaining why legacy drifted from unified storage; only a counter changes. The goroutine should log the error with the object/name context.

findings.title: Delete installs the base logger into the context instead of the enriched one
findings.body: `Delete` builds `log` with name/kind/method values but then calls `klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)` with the base logger, discarding those values for anything downstream that uses `klog.FromContext(ctx)` (including the legacy delete in the goroutine). Every other method installs the enriched `log`. Use `klog.NewContext(ctx, log)`.

findings.title: Mode 3 playlist tests read from the legacy API immediately after async legacy writes, which is inherently racy
findings.body: In mode 3, writes go to unified storage synchronously and to legacy only in a background goroutine with up to a 10s timeout. However `doPlaylistTests` (used by the new 'file, mode 3' and 'unified storage, mode 3' subtests) asserts legacy API state synchronously right after k8s writes: `/api/playlists` list must contain the just-created items (lines 523-531) and `getFromBothAPIs` does GET `/api/playlists/{uid}` immediately after create/update. Because the legacy write may not have completed yet, these assertions are timing-dependent and will flake, especially under load or CI. The tests need polling/waiting (e.g. require.Eventually) for legacy visibility in mode 3, or the dual writer needs a synchronous/blocked legacy write for testability.
